name: RLR³
title: Reinforcement Learning with Robust Rubric Rewards
authors: Ya-Qi Yu, Hao Wang, Fangyu Hong, Xiangyang Qu, et al.
intro: Extending rubric feedback into online learning: execute each criterion faithfully, preserve its signal, and prevent additional credit from compensating for essential failures.
figure_caption: RLR³ overview. Rubric construction, minimal-exposure execution, generative reward modeling, and policy optimization.
alt: Paper overview of RLR3: rubrics route criteria through extraction and deterministic verification or fuzzy judging, followed by reward aggregation and policy RL.
result_note: Reported on Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B. Each row compares methods within the same training mixture.

details.title: Execute with minimal exposure
details.text: Verifiable criteria use a text-only extractor followed by a deterministic verifier. Target arguments remain hidden from the extractor. Fuzzy criteria use a text-only judge with their grounding reference. Both paths exclude the source image.

details.title: Preserve essential failures
details.text: Decoupled normalization operates criterion by criterion across a response group. Hierarchical aggregation then gates the normalized reward: one essential score below 0.5, or at least two essential scores below 1, blocks content reward. A separate format mask handles response-level violations.

details.title: Toward a common model foundation
details.text: The open-source rubric-generator experiment initializes the generator from the same checkpoint as the policy and GenRM.

scope: Rubric execution combines criterion-level verification with essential-aware reward aggregation.

name: rDPO
title: Visual Preference Optimization with Rubric Rewards
authors: Ya-Qi Yu, Fangyu Hong, Xiangyang Qu, Hao Wang, et al.
intro: Establishing reusable rubric supervision: build an offline instruction–rubric pool, score target-policy responses, and select preference pairs that reflect task-relevant quality differences.
figure_caption: rDPO overview. Seed mining, rubric drafting, and on-policy preference-data curation for DPO.
alt: Paper overview of rDPO showing seed mining, checklist-style rubric construction and on-policy preference pair filtering.
result_note: Public downstream evaluation. The contribution is preference-data construction and filtering; the optimization objective is standard DPO.

details.title: Build once, reuse across policies
details.text: Seed mining retains disagreement-rich instructions. Independent rubric drafts are aggregated into essential and additional criteria. This offline instruction–rubric pool can support response generation from different target policies.

details.title: Score repeatedly, select deliberately
details.text: Each candidate is scored three times, using a per-criterion median. Essential qualification controls chosen and rejected eligibility; weighted rewards enforce a margin. Up to four maximum-margin pairs are selected per instruction, with each unique response appearing at most twice.

details.title: Separate task quality from style recovery
details.text: The private scaling setting includes response-style constraints. rDPO recovers the prompting-induced degradation and exceeds the unconstrained base average; the full gain over prompting should not be interpreted as an unqualified reasoning gain.

scope: Public and private settings serve different validation purposes. No empirical superiority over online GRPO is established by this study.
